:::{#cor-qp-sensitivity}
#### The multiplier is the sensitivity of the minimum value

In @thm-qp-equality, write the minimum value as a function of $\vecf{b}$,
$f^*(\vecf{b}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vecf{b}} \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}$. Then

$$
\deriv{\vecf{b}} f^*(\vecf{b}) = \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b} = -\vecf{\lambda}^*.
$$

:::

::: proof

$\matr{M}^{-1}$ is symmetric and does not depend on $\vecf{b}$, so

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vecf{b}} f^*(\vecf{b})
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2 \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(@thm-quadratic-form, with } \matr{M}^{-1} \text{ in place of } \matr{S} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{M}^{-1} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(simplify)}
\\
&= -\vecf{\lambda}^*.
&& \text{(definition of } \vecf{\lambda}^* \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-qp-sensitivity}
#### Moving the line

In @exm-qp-equality with a general right side $b$ in place of $5$,
$\matr{M}^{-1} = \tfrac{2}{25}$ and $f^*(b) = \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot \tfrac{2}{25}\,b^2 = \tfrac{b^2}{25}$,
so $\dif{}{b} f^*(b) = \tfrac{2b}{25}$.
At $b = 5$ this is $\tfrac{10}{25} = 0.4 = -\lambda^*$:
moving the line $3 x_1 + 4 x_2 = b$ outward by a small step $\varepsilon$ in $b$
raises the minimum value by about $0.4\,\varepsilon$.

:::
